source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: The lack of genitive case in Sakha and the obligatory presence of the dummy noun in possessor predicates
notes: However, this genitive relict in Sakha does not have the same function as its Turkish counterpart. In Turkish genitive possessors can be used predicatively (4b), Sakha nominative possessors cannot (4d). In order for a possessor to be predicated of its possessum, it must appear together with an empty noun kien devoid of lexical content as shown in (4e).
